about:
Cass County Electric Cooperative is headquartered in Fargo, North Dakota, and has operated as a member-owned electric cooperative since 1937. The organization was formed to bring reliable electricity to rural communities in southeastern North Dakota and remains owned by the members it serves.

The cooperative distributes electricity across a service territory that spans 10 counties, maintaining nearly 6,000 miles of distribution line and 41 substations. It provides power to nearly 61,000 members, including residential, commercial, agricultural, and apartment accounts. Beyond delivery, the cooperative offers member services such as outage monitoring, bill payment, service start/stop/transfer, energy conservation programs, and safety education.

Its customer base includes residential urban and farm accounts, commercial businesses, irrigation operations, and lighting services. The cooperative also supports the broader community through programs like Operation Round Up, which funds local organizations, scholarships and youth programs, and partnerships with community events across its service area.

The cooperative distinguishes itself through its not-for-profit, member-governed structure. A locally elected board of directors sets policy, and the organization emphasizes safety, integrity, innovation, accountability, and community investment as core values. Profits are returned to members as capital credits, and decisions are made with long-term community benefit in mind.
